subject: Post-call recap: on-prem/VPC constraints, data residency and next steps
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@averyhealth.com>, David Ortiz <d.ortiz@averyhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-22T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: on-prem/VPC constraints, data residency and next steps

Hi Priya / David —

Thanks for the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery + the concrete asks we captured so we can align next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you described
- Must keep PHI and related model inputs inside Avery’s US-only VPC / on-prem cluster for regulatory and internal policy reasons.
- Current inference experiments on cloud test instances are fine for eval but cannot be used for production due to residency and logging constraints.
- Need deterministic latency under 300ms for the triage use case; batching has to be carefully limited.

Goals
- Pilot Redwood Private on an isolated cluster (air-gapped option preferred) for the clinical triage workflow by end of Q2.
- Validate integration with Avery SSO + customer KMS and confirm audit/logging exports to your SIEM.
- Demonstrate no egress of unanonymized PHI from the cluster and document tracing for compliance.

Constraints / technical must-haves we captured
- No outbound internet for inference nodes (egress blocked).
- Allow-listing will be done at the org firewall; we will need an IP set for scheduled updates.
- Proxy for package updates only via curated internal mirror (no direct yum/apt to internet).
- Persistent KV cache must be stored on customer-provisioned encrypted storage behind KMS policies.

Attachments I’m sharing
- Avery_Env_Diagram.png — rough diagram from our whiteboard during the call
- SOC2_A-answers.pdf — Redwood’s high-level answers to Avery’s SOC2 questions we discussed (starter doc)
- onprem_network_matrix.xlsx — template for network and proxy details (please populate where possible)

Immediate next steps
1) You to share a filled network matrix with firewall/IPs and proxy details (David or your infra team).
2) Marcus to propose a minimal test-plan for an isolated proof-of-concept (POC) including a 2-week soak and latency checks.
3) Laura and I to coordinate legal + procurement kickoff for a PO deployment order form after tech fit confirmed.

Proposed timeline
- Network matrix back to us: within 3 business days
- Redwood POC proposal (technical runbook + infra requirements): 4 business days after we receive the matrix
- POC start target: week of 2027-04-12 (flexible based on your windows)

Who’s responsible (RACI-lite)
- Avery infra (David): network matrix, whitelist windows, local storage details
- Avery security (Priya): data residency sign-off and compliance checklist
- Redwood SE (Marcus): POC runbook and test harness
- Redwood AE (Laura): procurement + contracting lead

If helpful I can schedule a short tech working session (30–45m) with Marcus + your infra to go over the network matrix line-by-line.

Thanks again — I’ll follow up with calendar invites once we have the matrix.

Best,
Naomi

Thanks Naomi — this aligns with what we discussed. A couple of clarifying points before we complete the matrix: 

1) Egress policy:
- Our intention is zero egress from inference hosts except to our logging collector (internal IP) and to a customer-managed package mirror for OS/patch updates.
- Is Redwood able to support image/patch updates via an offline bundle (we can host) instead of direct internet pull?

2) KV cache persistence:
- We can provide an NFS-backed encrypted volume with our KMS. Does Redwood need a specific filesystem or can it work with ext4/xfs over NFS?

3) Latency: we will need a short list of sequence lengths and typical prompt sizes (tokens) to set realistic SLAs — happy to share sample payloads after the matrix.

I attached an internal network matrix that already has a few internal entries filled. Please have Marcus review the proxy and port rows.

Priya

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@averyhealth.com>, David Ortiz <d.ortiz@averyhealth.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-22T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: on-prem/VPC constraints, data residency and next steps

Hi Priya — thanks for the matrix, that’s super helpful. Quick technical notes and asks (short bullets):

- Offline updates: yes, we can support an offline bundle approach. Redwood will provide signed tarball bundles for runtime & model binaries; you can host them on your internal mirror. We will need a sync mechanism (scp/sftp) or an API endpoint inside your network to push bundles.
- Filesystem for cache: Redwood supports xfs/ext4 for local SSD-backed volumes. For NFS we recommend mounting with NFSv4 and disabling root_squash for performance; we can also support an object-backed store (S3-compatible) if you prefer.
- Ports: For the POC we need these minimal ports opened between Redwood control-plane proxies (customer-provided) and the management jump host: TCP 443 outbound from management host only; no persistent inbound open to internet. Runtime nodes should allow outbound to internal logging collector on TCP 514/udp and to your package mirror on TCP 22 or 443 depending on mirror config.
- Certificate management: we can accept customer-supplied certs (PKCS#12) for TLS termination on the gateway.

POC test plan outline (I'll put together the details in a runbook but summary here):
- Deploy runtime in isolated network (no internet) with customer-provided bundle
- Run synthetic traffic that mirrors your triage workloads (sample payloads requested)
- Measure tail latency and p99s across 72h soak; target p99 < 300ms
- Verify logs and audit export to your SIEM, confirm no PHI egress

Action items for Priya / David
- Confirm preferred package mirror protocol (scp vs https) and credentials method
- Confirm NFS vs object store for cache persistence
- Provide a 2-hour maintenance window for initial deploy (suggested: Friday 03/26 02:00–04:00 local)

I’ll assemble the runbook and share a link by EOD tomorrow.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
